rules.check: Each nontrivial implementation source file maps to exactly one unit-test file unless the user explicitly authorizes omission; documentation, agent instructions, declarative review registries, agent configuration, and demonstrably trivial glue are exempt.
Each nontrivial source class maps to exactly one test class; only demonstrably trivial glue is exempt.
Each unit test mocks external dependencies at the imported subject boundary, using `mock.patch.object()` when patching object members.
Every changed skipped test has explicit user authorization and a tracking ticket or explanation.
Each unit test without `subTest` contains exactly one ordered `# Arrange`, `# Act`, `# Assert` cycle.
Each unit-test name follows `test_<action>_<condition>_<expected_outcome>` and states concrete behavior.
Each unit test asserts a specific observable behavior rather than only non-null or no-throw execution.

sources.section: What is Not a Good Test

rules.check: Every changed executable behavioral branch has a unit test covering its outcome unless the user explicitly authorizes omission.
Each `subTest` case has an identifying title and its own independent Arrange, Act, and Assert cycle.
Each changed test proves consumer behavior without copying implementation logic or repository declarations into expected values.

sources.section: What is Not a Good Test

rules.check: Each changed unit test remains deterministic in the full suite without ordering assumptions, leaked mutable state, arbitrary sleeps, or retries.

sources.section: What is Not a Good Test

rules.check: Command tests exercise `do()` and `undo()` in separate test methods.
Tests expecting exceptions use `self.assertRaises` or `self.assertRaisesRegex`, never manual `try`/`except` flags.
